data.name: Aniketa
data.gender_notes: Aniketa is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Ani- (free from) + keta (obstacles). This name signifies freedom from all hindrances and obstacles, leading to a path of spiritual growth. The name Aniketa carries the meaning “Free from obstacles” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Aniketa usually hope their child will grow to embody free from obstacles and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name that encourages overcoming challenges and staying focused on one's spiritual journey.
data.etymology: Aniketa belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Free from obstacles.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Aniketa total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

data.cultural_impact: Aniketa is a Sanskrit name, derived from ancient Indian texts and scriptures. It has strong roots in Hinduism and holds a deep cultural significance. Historically, Hindu mythology is rich with stories of gods and goddesses who have bestowed their blessings upon individuals seeking liberation from worldly concerns and obstacles. Aniketa, as a name, represents this timeless principle and serves as an inspiration for those embarking on a spiritual journey.
data.spiritual_significance: Aniketa is a beacon of hope and encouragement for those seeking inner peace and freedom from worldly distractions. The name is rooted in the fundamental belief that through persistent effort and dedication, one can emerge victorious over life's challenges and obstacles. In spiritual terms, Aniketa represents the ultimate goal of Moksha (salvation) - the liberation from the cycle of birth, death, and rebirth. It's a reminder that inner peace and enlightenment can only be achieved when we are free from external hindrances and distractions.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Aniketa: One who is beyond the boundaries of illusion and maya. A soul that has transcended the limitations of the material world, seeking absolute union with the divine.

historical_references.reference: Aniketa was a famous sage and warrior who lived during the Mahabharata era. He is known for his prowess in battle and his devotion to Lord Krishna. Aniketa led an army of warriors against the Kauravas and was eventually killed in battle by Bhishma.
Aniketa was also a revered sage in ancient India who was known for his wisdom and knowledge of the Vedas. He is said to have authored several important texts on Hindu philosophy and religion.
